lesson_title: Nobody Sucks Air In: The Balloon-in-a-Bottle Truth About Breathing
hook_text: Your lungs have no muscles. So who is doing the breathing? Not your lungs.
clip_script: There is an upside-down tree in your chest. The trunk is your windpipe. Two branches, the bronchi. Thousands of twigs, the bronchioles. And on every twig, a bunch of grapes: the alveoli, 300 million of them, half a tennis court of surface, each wrapped in blood vessels. The nose cleans, warms and wets the air before it gets there. Now the breathing, and here is the surprise: the lungs have no muscles. They are two balloons in a box. Pull the floor of the box down, that is your diaphragm flattening, lift the ribs up and out, and the box gets bigger. Bigger box, lower pressure, and the outside air pushes in. Nobody sucks. Relax, the box shrinks, air flows out. Muscles, volume, pressure, air, always in that order. What comes out is different: oxygen down from 21 to 16 percent, carbon dioxide up a hundredfold to 4 percent, warm and wet enough to fog a window. Asthma tightens the twigs. TB eats the tree, six months of pills cures it. Smoking paralyses the cleaning hairs and pops the grapes. Keep the tree clean.
visual_style: A tree flips upside down into a rib cage; the trunk, branches and grape clusters light up in turn; a balloon inside a bottle inflates as a rubber sheet is pulled down; a window fogs with exhaled percentages.
pacing: Quick tree tour, a slow emphatic beat on 'nobody sucks', a rapid percentages beat, a hard finish on smoking.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and describe a breath in the four-step order.
